analysis.title: International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 2, 2026)
key_insights: Crude's move on Middle East diplomatic progress was mostly positioning-driven, with crude at the 100th percentile in JPM's CTA framework. Oil moved more than equities, rates or betting odds.
Resumption of combat operations after the US midterms is still consensus and likely, but JPM says it may prove brief and limited, without major fallout to regional energy infrastructure.
Iran's oil revenues are on track to hit zero by December for the first time, which JPM cites as an incentive for both sides to reach a deal.

Geopolitical improvement would benefit international equities more than US equities. EU/Japan natural gas now costs a record 12x the North American price, a ratio not reached in the 2022 gas shock or in 2011-2012.
The late-session US sell-off spilled into Asia. The TWSE index fell 3.6% as local investors unwound, and China's market support measures gained little traction while CNH had a multi-sigma drop.

JPM says a Soft Blue Wave is already priced in. Global semis sentiment is capitulatory, the SOX/SPX drawdown rivals 2008, and global AI infra effectively prices in stalling AI capex. In that scenario JPM expects equities to rise, AI infra to see relief and post-midterm seasonality to kick in.
A Big Blue Wave is a risk for Tech, especially if Abbott loses in Texas, where most AI infrastructure is being built. More local AI regulation would add to adverse reflexivity in the AI infra trade.

JPM argues that midterm risk to AI regulation is mostly state-level. A federal AI law is unlikely because Trump would veto it and Democrats cannot reach a 2/3 majority in both chambers. Tariff policy is unlikely to change, and a Democratic House could defund Middle East military efforts.
APAC clients are more bearish than US clients but less bearish than EU clients. Many APAC clients are up double digits on the year and lack incentive to re-engage until a clear trend emerges.

JPM sees the US consumer as robust. The top 4 income quintiles hold 6% to 27% more real cash than at YE2019 (nearly $8T nominal), and retail sales run $723bn a month YTD2026 versus $505bn in 2019. Credit card delinquencies are normalizing to pre-COVID trends, not deteriorating.

Consumer sub-sector views: airlines, cruise and hotels have robust demand. Autos and homebuilders are rate-sensitive, and parts and suppliers may be a better expression. Retailers face freight costs that are 30-40% of total cost and have more than tripled YTD. Staples are most at risk of margin compression and likely remain a source of funds.

AI infrastructure has absorbed more than $500B of debt YTD (IG above $350B, leveraged above $60B, private credit and structured about $100B+). The HY compute index is +372bps YTD. Hyperscaler all-in funding costs are up about 120bps, and credit is becoming more discriminating but there is no broader funding crisis.

AI-related CDS spreads have widened on technical selling and bank hedging of data center lending exposure, pushing CDS above cash-bond spreads. JPM sees positive-basis names as attractive for investors willing to sell protection. CRWV has converts outstanding and CDS at a slightly positive basis.

ORCL and SpaceX credit spreads widened significantly on reports each is seeking off-balance-sheet financing. JPM IG credit expects rising debt supply to pressure spreads into 2027, and says Nvidia is a key transmission channel for financial stress because of its links to GPU customers including CRWV.

JPM HY credit analyst Tom Egan calls CRWV a financing challenge, not a solvency one. He projects last-12-month EBITDA rising from about $4.4B (June 2026) to $7.3B by YE and nearly $20B by YE27, with about $130B of contracted revenue.

JPM views France as an idiosyncratic story, not a sovereign crisis 2.0. France's primary deficit is about 3% and debt/GDP about 120%, versus a 180% threshold JPM says is 10-15 years away. OATs discount debt/GDP above 150% and an implied deficit above 8%. JPM sees relief into year-end around the budget but no material reversal until the 2Q27 elections.
JPM says EU Banks earnings trends are unchanged and dips of more than 15% versus the index should be bought. It sees call ratio spreads and call spreads as attractive.

On Treasuries, before the Oct 22 rally the view was that 5.50% was more likely than 5.00% for the 10-year yield. The market prices a December 2026 hike and two in FY27, and clients see upside risk to that pricing. The downside risk is a near-term end to the US/Iran conflict with oil normalizing, held with low conviction.

Client discussion on tech: pushback on the semis bull case is that supply-chain-driven price spikes are unsustainable. Neoclouds face bankruptcy risk, though hyperscalers would likely buy at pennies on the dollar. Software is unlikely to be a funding source, and security and infra software are consensus longs. A buy needs a positioning flush, hyperscaler capex confirmation, semis earnings, tighter credit and positive seasonality, pointing to early November.

Broadening: since the July 28 lows the SPX is +4.8% (through Oct 22), but 69% of stocks lag the index. This makes it hard to pick a single stock and hedge with a sector ETF. Clients said an everything rally is possible short-term but not longer-term, with Tech dominating once the market stabilizes.

JPM's tactical equity stance is bullish: long US and Asia (Japan, Korea, Taiwan) versus EU. Longs: infrastructure, semi cap, less-levered hyperscalers, AI-vulnerable software and applications, EU and JA banks, EU industrials, JA machinery, GE Infra, EU miners, EU Pharma, UKX. Shorts: AI-vulnerable ex-software, short-cycle data center capex names, EU insurance, autos, chemicals, Asian consumer electronics, MedTech and MDAX.

JPM is bullish on EM. Tactical longs: China Star 50 versus KWEB, Korea versus South East Asia, and Taiwan. Hedges: long Brazil (EWZ) and EM (EEM). EM has recovered over 9% of its drawdown since end-July.

JPM Prime data shows October was a poor month for hedge funds. Global HF net returns were about -2.6% MTD through Oct 29 (likely about -3.5% after Friday), with a -2.2% long-short spread. Prior -3z events saw positive forward 20d spreads in 6 of 7 cases (avg +1%). Momentum exposure is at 12-month-plus lows.

US tactical positioning is at the 33rd percentile, retail sentiment at the 6th percentile, and CTA US equity positioning at the 44th percentile. TMT versus Defensives sentiment is at the 6th percentile, echoing prior lows that were followed by Tech-led rebounds. HFs flipped to buying biotech and medtech, kept selling utilities, and remain net long banks. EU positioning rebounded from the 5th to the 14th percentile, while China/HK positioning is at the 5th percentile.

market_movers.rationale: JPM says CRWV's challenge is financing, not solvency. Its CDS trades at a slightly positive basis and it has converts outstanding.
Credit spreads widened significantly on reports it is seeking off-balance-sheet financing, and externally-financed names have underperformed.
JPM IG credit calls Nvidia an important transmission channel for financial stress because of its interconnected relationships with GPU customers.
JPM likes long Brazil as a hedge on a potential structural policy shift and as a diversifier against weakness in the EM AI theme.

sector_views.rationale: Key longs across infrastructure, less-levered hyperscalers and AI-vulnerable software, while shorting ex-software AI-vulnerable and short-cycle data center capex names.
Earnings trend is unchanged and dips of more than 15% versus the index should be bought.
Most at risk of margin compression and likely to remain a source of funds.
Clients are negative because a Blue Wave could halt a military funding spike, though a lame-duck military funding bill could surprise to the upside.
Rates-sensitive with affordability pressure, so parts and suppliers may be a better way to play the group.

earnings_insights: Of SPX companies, about 65% mentioned AI improving operations in 26Q2 earnings, but fewer than 5% quantified the impact.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Clients see upside risk to rates based on household and corporate balance sheets, accelerating growth and inflation.

macro_indicators.reading: Hike in Dec 2026, then 2 hikes in FY27
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing is the baseline for equity investors. Fed DOTS show no hikes in FY27 and cuts in FY28 and FY29.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A record ratio, higher than the 2022 gas shock or 2011-2012.

trade_ideas.description: Long EU Banks on dips of more than 15% versus the index, using call ratio spreads and call spreads
trade_ideas.rationale: EU Banks earnings trend is unchanged and the tape echoes the 2011-12 sovereign crisis without a change in fundamentals.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically long China Star 50 versus China Internet (KWEB)
trade_ideas.rationale: Captures more innovative and AI-exposed names while large-cap internet is more exposed to Chinese consumers.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically long Korea versus South East Asia (ASEA)
trade_ideas.rationale: Expresses the AI winners versus losers view.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically long Taiwan after the Global Tech selloff in July
trade_ideas.rationale: Taiwan offers a less volatile exposure to AI and Asia Tech than Korea.
Potential structural policy shift, diversifies against EM AI weakness and is resilient to geopolitical risk.
trade_ideas.risk: Second-round presidential vote is at the end of the month.

trade_ideas.description: Long EM (EEM) for exposure to potential broadening
trade_ideas.rationale: Continued global macro strength, AI capex tailwinds and room for policy easing.

trade_ideas.description: Keep MCX < UKX option hedge and short France versus EU Domestics
trade_ideas.rationale: Pending clarity on spending, pragmatism and ideology, and on politics and dislocation in France.

trade_ideas.description: Sell CDS protection on AI names trading at positive basis, e.g. CRWV
trade_ideas.rationale: CDS spreads are above comparable cash-bond spreads because banks are buying protection to hedge data center lending.
trade_ideas.risk: Spreads may stay under pressure as debt supply grows into 2027.

risk_factors: Resumption of combat operations in the Middle East after the US midterms.
AI capex stalling, and growing AI infrastructure debt issuance and interconnected financing.
Further HF de-grossing, including Quant de-grossing, and elevated US Tech flows and futures positioning.
US Blue Wave outcomes, especially an Abbott loss in Texas and more state-level AI regulation.
French fiscal concerns and EGB spread widening.
Rising rates for leveraged GPU and data center financing, and delivery delays on compute capacity.
Freight cost increases of more than 3x YTD hurting retailers.

tension_points.bull_case: A Soft Blue Wave is priced in. Semis sentiment is capitulatory, the SOX/SPX drawdown rivals 2008, and JPM expects equities to rise and AI infra to rally with post-midterm seasonality.
tension_points.bear_case: A Big Blue Wave is a risk for Tech, especially if Abbott loses in Texas where most AI infrastructure is being built, adding adverse reflexivity to AI infra.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Abbott losing in Texas, or a Big Blue Wave producing more state-level AI regulation.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers are fundamentally well positioned, capital remains available and the HY compute index is +372bps YTD. CRWV has about $130b of contracted revenue.
tension_points.bear_case: Growing debt issuance, interconnected financing, higher borrowing costs and delivery risk constrain leveraged GPU and data center developers. Neocloud turmoil may spread to the whole group.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further widening in spreads for externally-financed names, or failure to deliver compute capacity on schedule.

tension_points.bull_case: France is idiosyncratic. The debt/GDP Rubicon of 180% is 10-15 years away, and the ECB backstop (TPI, OMT) limits disorderly spread widening.
tension_points.bear_case: The tape echoes the 2011-12 sovereign crisis, with EGB spreads wider and EUR and EU Banks lower. French bonds are crowded and 60% held by non-residents.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A breakdown in EGB spread stability, which JPM says is needed for EU broadening to gain conviction.
